idiom_name: @Serializable message data class plus extension-function mapper invoked by the listener
implementation_notes: The wire half belongs to kotlinx.serialization: the message is a separate @Serializable data class with @SerialName for wire names, and the mapper is one extension function per direction - fun Order.toMessage(): OrderMessage and fun OrderMessage.toDomain(): Order - called by the listener (a MessageListener, a Kafka ConsumerRecord handler, a coroutine dispatcher) so neither the domain class nor the message class knows the other exists. Generated serializers replace hand-written encoding; the structural half (customer: Customer flattened to customerId, money to minor units, identity resolution on the way in) stays in the extension functions, which is why the pattern is library-supported rather than absorbed.
pitfalls: kotlinx.serialization needs the message class, not the aggregate, to be serializable: annotating the domain type drags every association into the schema and publishes the model by accident.
Default values in a @Serializable constructor make absent fields silently legal, and encodeDefaults/explicitNulls settings decide what the wire actually carries - pin them so absence stays explicit.
Kotlin nullability is erased at runtime: a wire payload can still deliver null for a non-null field and throw SerializationException deep inside the decoder - validate at the boundary.
Property order and naming strategies can change the serialised payload after a refactor; keep wire names in @SerialName rather than relying on namingStrategy.
